stories.title: Climate change linked to rising preterm births in India
stories.summary: An exceptionally hot April in 2024 was associated with 10,050 additional preterm births in India. Research group Zero Carbon Analytics suggests that by mid-century, climate change could drive 15,300 excess preterm births during an ordinary April. The environment is becoming a public health variable.

stories.title: Supreme Court asks NMC to review mandatory rural service
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has directed the National Medical Commission to examine the issue of mandatory rural service for doctors following the completion of their MBBS degrees. A bench of Justices P S Narasimha and Alok Aradhe issued the order while hearing a petition regarding the policy.

stories.title: Health Ministry proposes immediate licence suspension for substandard drugs
stories.summary: The Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has proposed amendments to the Drugs Rules to allow for the immediate suspension of manufacturing licences for drugs declared not of standard quality. The move aims to eliminate regulatory delays that previously kept non-compliant batches on pharmacy shelves.

stories.title: Supreme Court questions relevance of two-child penalties
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has observed that laws penalising families for having more than two children have lost their relevance due to India's falling fertility rate. A bench led by Justice P S Narasimha suggested that the fear of overpopulation has crumbled alongside demographic changes.

stories.title: Delhi air quality reaches severe levels ahead of Diwali
stories.summary: Delhi recorded a severe air quality index at 18 monitoring stations, with AIIMS reaching 402 and Jahangirpuri hitting 459. Experts warn that weakening wind speeds and unfavourable weather conditions threaten to worsen the pollution crisis as the city prepares for Diwali celebrations.

stories.title: India accuses beverage giants of misleading labelling
stories.summary: India's food regulator has accused PepsiCo and Monster Beverage of using the energy drink label to dupe consumers. The legal battle serves as a test for the regulator's authority to police product marketing in a market projected to reach 1.6 billion dollars by 2028.

stories.title: Government proposes immediate suspension of manufacturing licences for substandard drugs
stories.summary: The Union Health Ministry has proposed amendments to the Drugs Rules, 1945, to allow immediate suspension of manufacturing licences for drugs declared not of standard quality. The government says the change aims to enable prompt regulatory intervention and ensure patient safety. The current process requires more steps.

stories.title: Centre proposes 10 new import gateways for drugs and medical devices
stories.summary: The Union Health Ministry has proposed adding 10 inland container depots, a special economic zone and an international airport to the list of authorised entry points for medical imports. The amendment to the Drugs Rules, 1945, aims to reduce inland transportation distances for healthcare products across the country.

stories.title: Enforcement Directorate freezes assets in counterfeit medicine investigation
stories.summary: The Directorate of Enforcement has conducted searches at five premises in Karnataka linked to an alleged counterfeit medicines racket. The agency has frozen a bank account containing approximately 9 lakh rupees. The investigation follows a joint raid by local police and the drug controlling authority in August.

stories.title: Delhi air quality hits very poor category as winter restrictions begin
stories.summary: Delhi air quality has reached the very poor category for the first time this winter, triggering Stage 2 of the Graded Response Action Plan. The measures mandate increased vehicle parking fees to discourage private car use. The last time the air reached this level was in February.

stories.title: WHO adds two vaccine candidates to Ebola trial
stories.summary: The World Health Organization has recommended adding ChAdOx1 and mRNA-1469 to the ongoing Tumaini clinical trial in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. These are the first vaccines specifically designed to protect against the Bundibugyo virus to be evaluated during an active outbreak of the disease.

stories.title: Bangladesh faces world's largest measles outbreak
stories.summary: Bangladesh has reported 202,000 suspected measles cases since March, according to the World Health Organization. The country, once recognised for its high childhood immunisation coverage, is now managing what the agency describes as the world's largest measles outbreak by suspected case count for this year.

stories.summary: A child in Lewis County has died after contracting measles, marking the first death from the disease in New York in 30 years. Governor Kathy Hochul linked the event to federal immunisation policies. The state is currently reviewing the circumstances of the case.

stories.summary: Remote wearable devices are increasingly used in decentralized clinical trials to capture continuous real-world data. One study found a 14-day adhesive ECG patch detected arrhythmias in 59.5 percent of patients, compared to 19 percent with a traditional 24-hour Holter monitor. Wearables are now filling the gaps between site visits.

stories.summary: Pune-based Clinics On Cloud has raised 120 crore rupees in Series A funding at a 600 crore rupee valuation. The company plans to use the capital from Dubai-based Model42 to expand its network of microclinics. Most startups raise money early and often, but this one waited eight years.

stories.title: Pembroke Regional Hospital joins shared digital health record system
stories.summary: Pembroke Regional Hospital has launched a digital health record system as part of the Atlas Alliance. The transition allows 18 healthcare organizations across Eastern Ontario to access shared patient information. The hospital went live with the Epic system on October 24 as part of the third wave of onboarding.

stories.title: Rare disease patients report high rates of mental health struggles
stories.summary: A survey of 500 people by Rare Barometer found seven in 10 individuals affected by rare diseases report poor mental health. Nearly half experienced symptoms of depression, six times the rate of the general UK population. Feelings of isolation were up to 20 times more common among respondents.

stories.title: University of Lincoln launches mental health research unit
stories.summary: The University of Lincoln has launched the Lincolnshire Unit for Mental Health Research with 10.96 million pounds in funding. The initiative aims to expand research capacity and strengthen collaboration between the NHS, local government, and academic institutions. The unit was formally launched on November 3.

stories.title: Salisbury University recognized for mental health resources
stories.summary: Salisbury University has been named to the Princeton Review 2027 Mental Health Services Honor Roll. The recognition, based on a survey of 76 universities, highlights institutions demonstrating dedication to student mental health. The survey was conducted in partnership with the Ruderman Family Foundation.

stories.title: Online communication patterns linked to adolescent well-being
stories.summary: A study of 3,034 Swedish 15-year-olds found that online communication impacts mental well-being differently based on friendship type. Intense communication with close friends was associated with better well-being, while communication with online-only friends was linked to poorer outcomes. Patterns vary by frequency and the nature of the connection.

stories.title: Australian study identifies circadian depression subtype
stories.summary: Researchers at the University of Sydney have identified a subtype of depression linked to internal body clock disruptions. The study of 15,000 people defined circadian disturbance criteria as potential markers for the condition. The team suggests these disturbances are a distinct clinical indicator for some patients.

stories.title: Online sports betting may affect mental health
stories.summary: A study from ConsumerAffairs suggests that online sports betting may come with a mental health cost. The full piece is for subscribers. Further details were thin in the open report.

stories.title: Early menopause and mental health
stories.summary: ConsumerAffairs reports that early menopause may come with a hidden mental health challenge. The full piece is for subscribers. Further details were thin in the open report.

stories.title: Rising temperatures may increase suicide risk
stories.summary: Research from Georgetown University and the World Bank links extreme heat to higher suicide risk by disrupting sleep and emotional regulation. The study identifies specific temperature thresholds associated with psychological distress. Extreme heat is now being studied for its impact on more than just physical exhaustion.

stories.title: Study links extreme heat to mental health decline
stories.summary: A World Bank and Georgetown University study published in Environmental Research suggests extreme heat increases suicide risk by disrupting sleep and emotional control. The research highlights the mental health effects of climate change. The weather is now being asked to account for its psychological impact.

stories.title: Global mental health scores are languishing
stories.summary: A survey of 50,000 people across 92 countries found that global mental health is currently languishing, particularly among younger generations. Researchers noted lower vitality and resilience in younger cohorts compared to older groups. The future is not the only thing causing concern for the youth.

research.summary: Scientists have discovered that a drug originally developed for spinal cord injuries can tackle several key features of Alzheimer’s disease, including DNA damage and inflammation. research.title: Scientists discover surprising heart benefits of eating avocado and mango every day
research.summary: Eating an avocado and a cup of mango every day may provide surprising benefits for heart health, according to a new study involving adults with prediabetes. After just eight weeks, participants experienced significant improvements in blood vessel function and diastolic blood pressure, particularly among men. These benefits occurred.

USC researchers found that an experimental drug restored aging liver cells in rats, cutting levels of an Alzheimer’s-linked protein in half and bringing bad cholesterol down to youthful levels.
